newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ITALIAN SERIE A MATCHES THIS WEEKEND.

text.p: Italian Serie A matches due to be played on Sunday (league positions in brackets, kick-off times GMT):

The midweek death of 22-year-old Atalanta striker Federico Pisano, killed in a car crash, will cast a shadow over one of the most in-form sides in the league, unbeaten since losing 3-1 to Bologna on November 24. As usual, Filippo Inzaghi and Gigi Lentini lead the Atalanta attack against a Vicenza side led by Uruguyan Marcelo Otero.

Juventus will be without suspended Uruguyan defender Paolo Montero as well as injured Croat striker Alen Boksic but should still have too much firepower for struggling Perugia. Alessandro Del Piero and Michele Padovano lead the Juventus attack while Brazilian striker Muller joins Croat Milan Rapajic in the Perugia front line.

In their second game under reappointed coach, 1982 World Cup hero Dino Zoff, Lazio look to a 4-4-2 line-up in which midfielders Czech Pavel Nedved and Diego Fuser provide attacking thrust. Inter, with only 13 points from a possible 33 since mid-November, look to Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff and Maurizio Ganz to pull off a badly-needed win.

Champions AC Milan are in a major crisis which may be prolonged by in-form Bologna. Liberian George Weah and Roberto Baggio lead the Milan attack while Carlo Nervo, Russian Igor Kolivanov and Swede Kennet Andersson reply for Bologna.

A full-strength Napoli led by Brazilian midfielder-cum-libero Andre Cruz, with Alfredo Aglietti and Nicola Caccia in attack and with Argentine Roberto Ayala and Belgian Bertrand Crasson in defence should prove too strong for all-Italian Piacenza.

Parma are the favourites in this keenly-felt Emilia Romagna derby. Bottom side Reggiana, with only one win all season, are led by Russian striker Igor Simutenkov while Parma trust to Enrico Chiesa in attack with midweek Wembley heroes Dino Baggio and Fabio Cannavaro in midfield and defence.

Sampdoria's Swedish coach Sven Eriksson has said that this game represents a test of maturity for his side who must face Roma without four key players in captain Roberto Mancini, goalkeeper Fabrizio Ferron and defender Emmanuele Pesaresi, all suspended, and injured defender Moreno Mannini. Roma will be led by Argentine striker Abel Balbo, who has scored 13 goals, but may not prove strong enough to stop a Sampdoria side that is unbeaten since December 8.

Brazilian Amoroso and Paolo Poggi lead the Udinese attack in this relegation battle. German striker Oliver Bierhoff, out since December 1, may start on the Udinese substitute's bench. Sandro Tovalieri will be the lone man up front for a Cagliari side looking for a vital away draw.

Despite beating Milan 3-1 three weeks ago, Verona remain stuck in second-to-last position and look unlikely to improve on that standing against Fiorentina. Filippo Maniero and Nicola Zanini lead the Verona attack while the former Everton and Manchester United winger, Russian Andrei Kanchelskis, makes his Italian league debut alongside Portugal's Rui Costa and Fiorentina's Argentine captain Gabriel Batistuta.
